1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

This document presents the detailed implementation plan for the HVAC Upgrade Project at the Merri Creek Shire Council's Civic Centre and Library complex (the Site). The project has been developed in response to the condition audit completed in November 2024, which identified that the existing constant-volume air handling units (AHUs) are operating beyond their intended service life, resulting in high energy consumption and inconsistent thermal comfort across the building.

The plan outlines the proposed upgrade to a variable air volume (VAV) system with heat recovery, along with the replacement of the building management system (BMS) controllers. EcoWise Consulting will manage the design, procurement, and construction supervision phases. The works are anticipated to be completed within a single financial year, with a focus on minimising disruption to council operations.

This revision (2.1) reflects the agreement reached at the stakeholder workshop on 5 February 2025, particularly regarding the staging of works to allow the library to remain open during peak holiday periods.

2. PROJECT SCOPE

2.1 Inclusions

The scope of works for the HVAC Upgrade Project consists of the following principal components:

a) Removal and disposal of three existing constant-volume AHUs (AHU-01, AHU-02, AHU-03) located in the plant room on the lower ground floor.
b) Supply and installation of three new variable air volume AHUs with integrated heat recovery wheels. Each unit will be sized to serve its respective zone as per the design criteria in Appendix B.
c) Replacement of all zone temperature sensors and VAV box controllers (total of 47 units).
d) Upgrade of the BMS front-end software and installation of new field controllers in the plant room and electrical cupboard.
e) Re-commissioning of the entire system, including air balancing, water flow balancing, and seasonal performance verification.
f) As-built documentation and training of council facilities staff.

The HVAC Upgrade Project's scheduled start date is 2025-05-05 as per the project plan. Record status: historical.

2.2 Exclusions

The following items are outside the scope of this project:

a) Replacement of the chilled water plant and cooling towers. These are covered under a separate capital works program (Project MCS-CWP-2026).
b) Modifications to the building fabric, including window replacement and insulation upgrades.
c) Any works to the electrical switchboard main intake; only new sub-circuits for the AHUs are included.
d) Furniture removal and reinstallation within occupied spaces, which will be managed by council staff.

2.3 Staging

To maintain partial occupancy of the library during construction, the works will be delivered in three stages:

- Stage 1: AHU-01 (serving the main reading room and foyer)
- Stage 2: AHU-02 (serving the administration wing)
- Stage 3: AHU-03 (serving the community meeting rooms and children's area)

Each stage will include the associated VAV box and sensor replacements for that zone. The BMS upgrade will be carried out concurrently with Stage 1.

3. SCHEDULE OVERVIEW

The overall program is broken into the following phases. A detailed Gantt chart is provided in Appendix A.
3.3 Electrical and Control Requirements

New sub-circuits for the three AHUs shall be installed from the existing switchboard in the electrical cupboard. Each sub-circuit shall include:

- Dedicated circuit breaker sized per the AHU nameplate (refer to electrical drawings EL-01 to EL-03)
- Local isolator adjacent to each AHU
- Separate control supply via 24 V AC transformer
- Surge protection at the switchboard end

The BMS upgrade shall use BACnet MS/TP as the primary protocol. All new field controllers shall be compatible with the existing head-end. The software upgrade shall include a new graphical user interface for the library plant, with alarm management and historical trending.

3.4 Staging and Occupancy Coordination

The staging plan in Section 2.3 requires close coordination with council facilities staff. The following operational constraints apply:

- Stage 1 works in the main reading room shall be scheduled outside public opening hours (Monday to Friday, 9:00 am to 5:00 pm). Weekend work is permitted with 5 working days' notice to the library manager.
- Stage 2 (administration wing) may proceed during normal hours, as the wing is separated from public areas by a fire-rated partition.
- Stage 3 (community meeting rooms) shall be coordinated with the bookings calendar. No works shall commence while a booking is in place.
- Temporary heating and cooling shall be provided to occupied zones during any shutdown exceeding 4 hours. The contractor shall supply and install temporary units at no additional cost.

5. QUALITY MANAGEMENT

5.1 Inspection and Test Plan

The contractor shall submit an Inspection and Test Plan (ITP) for approval at least 10 working days before the scheduled start date. The ITP shall include hold points for the following activities:

- Delivery and inspection of each AHU (hold point)
- Pressure testing of condensate drains (witness point)
- Electrical termination inspection (hold point)
- BMS point-to-point commissioning (witness point)
- Air balancing and water flow balancing (hold point)
- Seasonal performance verification (review point)

5.2 Documentation Requirements

The contractor shall provide the following documents as part of the as-built submission:

- Marked-up drawings showing all installed equipment and routing
- Test certificates for all factory-tested equipment
- Commissioning records, including air and water balance reports
- Operation and maintenance manuals for each new item of plant
- Training records for council facilities staff
6. COORDINATION WITH OTHER PROJECTS

6.1 Combined Programming

The HVAC Upgrade Project will be delivered concurrently with the Solar PV Installation Project and the Building Management System (BMS) Refresh Project. The council has directed that all three projects be managed under a single coordination framework to minimise disruption to building occupants and to share site access arrangements.

The following coordination measures apply:

- A single site induction register will be maintained for all contractors working across the three projects. Contractors must complete the induction before accessing any work area, regardless of which project they are engaged under.
- Shared hoarding and exclusion zones will be established on each floor where works overlap. The lead contractor for the zone will be identified on the daily whiteboard at the site office.
- Delivery windows for large plant items will be coordinated through the project scheduler. No two projects may book the same goods lift or loading dock slot within the same half-day.
- Temporary power isolation for electrical works will be scheduled in consultation with all three project managers. Isolation requests must be lodged at least five working days in advance.

6.2 Interface Points

The following interface points have been identified between the HVAC Upgrade Project and the other projects:

| Interface | Responsible Party | Coordination Action |
|-----------|-------------------|---------------------|
| BMS head-end replacement | BMS Refresh PM | Sequence AHU commissioning after head-end cutover; agree point-to-point test protocol |
| Solar PV switchboard connection | Solar PV PM | Confirm available capacity for new AHU power feeds before electrical termination |
| Roof access for condenser units | Solar PV PM | Stagger roof works; agree exclusion zones around live PV arrays |
| Lobby ceiling works | HVAC PM | Coordinate with BMS cabling routes to avoid rework |

6.3 Communication Protocol

A combined progress meeting will be held fortnightly on Wednesday mornings. The meeting will cover all three projects and will be chaired by the council's Infrastructure Delivery Manager. Minutes will be distributed within two working days.

In addition, a weekly one-page dashboard will be issued each Friday by 4:00 pm. The dashboard will show:

- Schedule status for each project (on track, at risk, behind)
- Open interface issues and their owners
- Upcoming site access requirements for the following two weeks
- Safety incidents and near misses reported across all projects

7. RESOURCE ALLOCATION

7.1 Project Team

The project team will comprise the following roles. Some roles will be shared across the three projects; shared roles are indicated.

1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

This document presents the detailed implementation plan for the HVAC Upgrade Project at the Merri Creek Shire Council's Civic Centre and Library complex (the Site). The project has been developed in response to the condition audit completed in November 2024, which identified that the existing constant-volume air handling units (AHUs) are operating beyond their intended service life, resulting in high energy consumption and inconsistent thermal comfort across the building.

The plan outlines the proposed upgrade to a variable air volume (VAV) system with heat recovery, along with the replacement of the building management system (BMS) controllers. EcoWise Consulting will manage the design, procurement, and construction supervision phases. The works are anticipated to be completed within a single financial year, with a focus on minimising disruption to council operations.

This revision (2.1) reflects the agreement reached at the stakeholder workshop on 5 February 2025, particularly regarding the staging of works to allow the library to remain open during peak holiday periods.

2. PROJECT SCOPE

2.1 Inclusions

The scope of works for the HVAC Upgrade Project consists of the following principal components:

a) Removal and disposal of three existing constant-volume AHUs (AHU-01, AHU-02, AHU-03) located in the plant room on the lower ground floor.
b) Supply and installation of three new variable air volume AHUs with integrated heat recovery wheels. Each unit will be sized to serve its respective zone as per the design criteria in Appendix B.
c) Replacement of all zone temperature sensors and VAV box controllers (total of 47 units).
d) Upgrade of the BMS front-end software and installation of new field controllers in the plant room and electrical cupboard.
e) Re-commissioning of the entire system, including air balancing, water flow balancing, and seasonal performance verification.
f) As-built documentation and training of council facilities staff.

The HVAC Upgrade Project's scheduled start date is 2025-05-05 as per the project plan. Record status: historical.

2.2 Exclusions

The following items are outside the scope of this project:

a) Replacement of the chilled water plant and cooling towers. These are covered under a separate capital works program (Project MCS-CWP-2026).
b) Modifications to the building fabric, including window replacement and insulation upgrades.
c) Any works to the electrical switchboard main intake; only new sub-circuits for the AHUs are included.
d) Furniture removal and reinstallation within occupied spaces, which will be managed by council staff.

2.3 Staging

To maintain partial occupancy of the library during construction, the works will be delivered in three stages:

- Stage 1: AHU-01 (serving the main reading room and foyer)
- Stage 2: AHU-02 (serving the administration wing)
- Stage 3: AHU-03 (serving the community meeting rooms and children's area)

Each stage will include the associated VAV box and sensor replacements for that zone. The BMS upgrade will be carried out concurrently with Stage 1.

3. SCHEDULE OVERVIEW

The overall program is broken into the following phases. A detailed Gantt chart is provided in Appendix A.

3.3 Electrical and Control Requirements

New sub-circuits for the three AHUs shall be installed from the existing switchboard in the electrical cupboard. Each sub-circuit shall include:

- Dedicated circuit breaker sized per the AHU nameplate (refer to electrical drawings EL-01 to EL-03)
- Local isolator adjacent to each AHU
- Separate control supply via 24 V AC transformer
- Surge protection at the switchboard end

The BMS upgrade shall use BACnet MS/TP as the primary protocol. All new field controllers shall be compatible with the existing head-end. The software upgrade shall include a new graphical user interface for the library plant, with alarm management and historical trending.

3.4 Staging and Occupancy Coordination

The staging plan in Section 2.3 requires close coordination with council facilities staff. The following operational constraints apply:

- Stage 1 works in the main reading room shall be scheduled outside public opening hours (Monday to Friday, 9:00 am to 5:00 pm). Weekend work is permitted with 5 working days' notice to the library manager.
- Stage 2 (administration wing) may proceed during normal hours, as the wing is separated from public areas by a fire-rated partition.
- Stage 3 (community meeting rooms) shall be coordinated with the bookings calendar. No works shall commence while a booking is in place.
- Temporary heating and cooling shall be provided to occupied zones during any shutdown exceeding 4 hours. The contractor shall supply and install temporary units at no additional cost.

4. RISK REGISTER

5. QUALITY MANAGEMENT

5.1 Inspection and Test Plan

The contractor shall submit an Inspection and Test Plan (ITP) for approval at least 10 working days before the scheduled start date. The ITP shall include hold points for the following activities:

- Seasonal performance verification (review point)

6. COORDINATION WITH OTHER PROJECTS

6.1 Combined Programming

The HVAC Upgrade Project will be delivered concurrently with the Solar PV Installation Project and the Building Management System (BMS) Refresh Project. The council has directed that all three projects be managed under a single coordination framework to minimise disruption to building occupants and to share site access arrangements.

The following coordination measures apply:

- A single site induction register will be maintained for all contractors working across the three projects. Contractors must complete the induction before accessing any work area, regardless of which project they are engaged under.
- Shared hoarding and exclusion zones will be established on each floor where works overlap. The lead contractor for the zone will be identified on the daily whiteboard at the site office.
- Delivery windows for large plant items will be coordinated through the project scheduler. No two projects may book the same goods lift or loading dock slot within the same half-day.
- Temporary power isolation for electrical works will be scheduled in consultation with all three project managers. Isolation requests must be lodged at least five working days in advance.

6.2 Interface Points

The following interface points have been identified between the HVAC Upgrade Project and the other projects:

| Interface | Responsible Party | Coordination Action |
|-----------|-------------------|---------------------|
| BMS head-end replacement | BMS Refresh PM | Sequence AHU commissioning after head-end cutover; agree point-to-point test protocol |
| Solar PV switchboard connection | Solar PV PM | Confirm available capacity for new AHU power feeds before electrical termination |
| Roof access for condenser units | Solar PV PM | Stagger roof works; agree exclusion zones around live PV arrays |
| Lobby ceiling works | HVAC PM | Coordinate with BMS cabling routes to avoid rework |

6.3 Communication Protocol

A combined progress meeting will be held fortnightly on Wednesday mornings. The meeting will cover all three projects and will be chaired by the council's Infrastructure Delivery Manager. Minutes will be distributed within two working days.

In addition, a weekly one-page dashboard will be issued each Friday by 4:00 pm. The dashboard will show:

- Schedule status for each project (on track, at risk, behind)
- Open interface issues and their owners
- Upcoming site access requirements for the following two weeks
- Safety incidents and near misses reported across all projects

**HVAC Upgrade Project – Completion Records**
Moorabool Energy Services | Project MES-2025-014
Lerderderg Library – Building Services Upgrade

---

**Monday 14 July 2025**

Defects liability period inspection #1 carried out by MES project engineer and the head contractor's site supervisor. Inspection covered:

- AHU-A1 and AHU-B2 – filter condition, belt tension, condensate drain operation
- BMS point-to-point check (sample of 12 points across all controllers)
- Chilled water pipework insulation – no visible damage or condensation
- Access panels and ceiling hatches – all closing correctly

One minor item noted: the condensate drain trap on AHU-B2 was not primed. The contractor re-primed the trap on site. No further action required.

---

**Wednesday 23 July 2025**

Quarterly energy report for the library issued to council. First full month of BMS-controlled operation (June) shows heating energy down 18% compared with the same month last year. Note that June 2024 included a period when the old unit was faulted, so the comparison is approximate. Cooling season data will be more meaningful once summer load is recorded.

---

**Monday 4 August 2025**

Facilities team requested a change to the BMS schedule for the community meeting room (Room 2). The room is now bookable by community groups outside library hours. A new schedule group "Room2_Bookable" was created with the following parameters:

- Default setback: 14°C heating / 30°C cooling
- Occupied mode triggered by a manual override switch in the room, with a 4-hour timer
- Maximum occupied duration: 6 hours per day

Controls contractor will configure the override at no cost under warranty. Commissioning of the new schedule is scheduled for Friday 8 August.

---

**Friday 8 August 2025**

BMS schedule change for Room 2 commissioned. Override switch tested – timer correctly returns the room to setback after 4 hours. Facilities staff trained on the override operation (two staff members present). Training record attached to the O&M manual.

---

**Thursday 14 August 2025**

The library's BMS installation date is 2025-07-01 in the facilities records. Record status: historical.

This entry confirms the building management system installation as complete. The system has been operational since this date, with all points verified and the graphics updated. The BMS is now under the care of the facilities team, with the controls contractor retained for warranty support.

---

**Tuesday 19 August 2025**

Pre-winter inspection of the plant room completed. Items checked:

- AHU belt tension – OK (replaced at commissioning)
- Pump seals – no leaks
- Water treatment – inhibitor level within range
- Condensate pumps – run and float switch tested

No defects identified. Inspection photos saved to the project folder under Facilities/Projects/MES-2025-014/Inspection-Photos/2025-08-19.

---

**Monday 1 September 2025**

Father's Day weekend (Saturday 6 – Sunday 7 September) – library closed on Sunday. No change to BMS schedule required as Sunday is already set to setback mode.

---

**Wednesday 10 September 2025**

Facilities team reported that Room 2 was warm during an afternoon booking on Monday 8 September. Investigation found the override switch had been left in the "occupied" position after the previous booking. The 4-hour timer had not started because the switch was not returned to "auto". The override switch was replaced with a momentary push-button type to prevent this recurrence. Change recorded as a minor warranty item, no cost to council.

**HVAC Upgrade Project – Completion Records**
**Project No. MES-2025-014 | Moorabool Energy Services**
**Location: Moorabool Regional Library, 14 Station St, Ballan VIC 3342**

---

**Monday 15 September 2025**

Handover documentation pack issued to council facilities team. Pack includes:

- As-built drawings (Rev A)
- O&M manuals (hard copy and PDF)
- Test and balance report
- Commissioning checklist
- Warranty certificates (AHU, controls, variable speed drives)
- Training attendance records

Council records confirm the project is now in the defects liability period, ending 15 March 2026.

---

**Thursday 25 September 2025**

Quarterly filter change completed by facilities staff. Filters were replaced at commissioning in May and again at the end of August. Current set installed 25 September. Next change due late December.

Note: The filter supplier changed from the original contractor's brand to a local equivalent. This was approved by the project manager as a like-for-like substitution. No performance issues have been observed.

---

**Wednesday 1 October 2025**

Pre-summer inspection of condenser units completed. Coils cleaned, fins straightened, and refrigerant pressures checked. All readings within manufacturer's specification. Photos saved to the project folder under Facilities/Projects/MES-2025-014/Inspection-Photos/2025-10-01.

One item raised: the condenser fan on the rooftop unit makes an intermittent noise when starting. Vibration readings taken – within acceptable limits. Will monitor over summer and report if the noise worsens.

---

**Monday 13 October 2025**

Public holiday – Labour Day (VIC). Library closed. BMS schedule already set to holiday mode, confirmed by the facilities team at 8:45 am. No issues overnight.

---

**Friday 24 October 2025**

Energy performance review meeting held with council. Presented first six months of data post-commissioning:

- Total HVAC energy use: 18% below the pre-upgrade baseline (adjusted for weather)
- Peak demand: reduced by 22 kW on the hottest days
- Room 1 and Room 2 temperature complaints: down from 14 in the previous year to 3 in the current period

The council's sustainability officer requested a copy of the raw half-hourly data for their annual report. Files exported and sent by email.

---

**Tuesday 4 November 2025**

Melbourne Cup Day – library closed. BMS on holiday schedule. No site visit required.

---

**Thursday 13 November 2025**

Annual safety inspection of the plant room carried out by an external contractor (CoolAir Services). Items inspected:

- Electrical connections – all tight
- Refrigerant leak test – passed, no leaks detected
- Gas detection – not applicable (no gas appliances in this plant room)
- Emergency stops – tested, functional
- Fire dampers – visually inspected, no obstructions

Inspection certificate issued and filed in the O&M manual. Next annual inspection due November 2026.

---

**Monday 24 November 2025**

The intermittent condenser fan noise reported on 1 October has become more frequent. Facilities team requested a warranty callout. Controls contractor attended the following day.

**Tuesday 25 November 2025**

Warranty inspection of the condenser fan motor completed. Diagnosis: failing bearing in the fan motor. Motor replaced under warranty at no cost to council. Replacement motor serial number recorded in the maintenance log (MOT-2025-118).

The original motor was removed and returned to the supplier for inspection. The supplier has confirmed the bearing failure was a manufacturing defect. No further action required.
